findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the kitchen would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Employees conducted troubleshooting on the equipment and the machine began functioning correctly prior to the inspector leaving. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are functioning correctly at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location.

A container labeled “seafood utensils” at a prep station was observed with standing water and floating debris in the bottom of the container. A nearby employee stated that it should be for clean utensils. The employee was shown and moved the container to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact utensils are maintained clean and protected from contamination until use.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Opened containers of milk and buttermilk are observed without date marking in the walk in cooler. The PIC indicated that they were likely opened last week and discarded them to correct the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are date marked once opened and discarded at the end of the seventh day.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area was without paper towels. The PIC was asked about paper towels and then replaced them during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

The bar manager worked on the machine for a few minutes and the machine registered correctly afterwards. Ensure that all sanitizers are at effective levels at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside of the spout for the soda gun at the left side of the bar has a black substance built up. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent soilage.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

A pan of portioned cooked spaghetti in the walk in cooler has a date marking of 7/17/25. Today is day 13 when the items should have been used or discarded by the end of day seven. The PIC checked the bags and agreed that they were old and discarded them during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are used or discarded by the end of day seven where the day of preparation is day one.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours.

A gallon of milk in the walk in cooler is observed partially used. The PIC indicated that it had been opened approximately 5 days ago. Education was conducted and a date placed on the container to correct. Ensure that these items are given date markings if they are going to be at the facility longer than 24 hours and used or discarded prior to the end of the 7th day.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed rusted and in need of repair. This can come in many forms but needs to have an end result of a smooth and easily cleanable surface. Repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Two of the three CFPMs at the facility are unable to show an allergen training certificate during this inspection. They are instructed to complete allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and maintain copies of the certificate at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Inspector observed three employees with personal drinks in the kitchen. The facility manager talked to the employees. One of the drinks had a lid and a straw and was down low as required. The other two were without lids or straws and improperly stored.  

(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the wait station to be soiled. Also the nozzle of the water dispenser at the wait station near the Liquor closet is soiled with mineral deposits. Clean and maintain these items clean. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Live roaches are observed in the back corner of the south server station. The facility recently switched pest control companies. The new company paperwork states that they are on monthly service. Inspector highly suggests more frequent service and monitoring to eliminate pests from the facility. Follow up will be conducted in 10 days.

PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: Inspector observed the base cove in the back right corner of the south server station with the pest issue to have base cove that is pulled away from the wall and a gap where the roaches are congregating. Clean and seal this area to deny the pests a place to live. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple drain flies at the bar during this inspection. The concentration of flies is at the area between the dish machine and the area with and ice bin, glass sprayer, and dipper well. The dry storage area is free of flies at this time. The facility has regular pest control. Inspector highly suggests putting into practice the advice of the pest control operator. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the floor drain at the bar to still have some soil in it around the edge where the pipe changes diameter. Ensure that all the areas of the drain are clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed both soda guns at the bar to be heavily soiled with mold. The same conditions existed at the last routine inspection on 9/8/23. Develop a habit of cleaning at the bar and maintaining the food contact surfaces properly cleaned and sanitized.
The soda guns were properly cleaned during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed soda guns to be heavily soiled with mold. Soda guns are a food contact surface. Soda is contaminated with mold as it passes through the soda dispenser. Properly clean and sanitize this food contact surface at lest once every 24hours. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cranberry juice labeled must refrigerate after opening and ZingZang stored in the bar wine cooler. The items were 45F when checked with a probe thermometer. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection. Do not use the wine cooler for juices or any other food item. Only food items that do not require refrigeration should be stored in the wine coolers as they do not hold at 41F or below. The cranberry juice and ZingZang were discarded.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed open cream in the bar glass front cooler lacking a date marking. Date all dairy and juice products. They are prepared,  TCS foods and require date marking. Cream was date marked. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed drain flies at the bar and dry storage back by the onions. The facility has regular pest control. Look into more effective methods to rid the facility of drain flies.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Caulking needs to be redone between the dish machine drain board and the wall. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.
